objective: We want more EMI-eligible card purchases to become EMI. We have no campaign history. I need a 7 day plan.
objectiveFingerprint: become campaign card day eligible emi history no plan purchases

questions.text: When you say you want more purchases to convert to EMI, what does winning look like for you: more transactions converted regardless of size, or converting the larger-ticket transactions specifically (since those carry more interest/fee value or risk)?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: If it's about the count of conversions, the campaign targets broadly across all EMI-eligible transactions and is judged on number of conversions.
contingency.ifB: If it's about value, the campaign prioritises and sequences around higher-ticket eligible transactions and is judged on value converted, not count.
contingency.thenA: Design targets all eligible transactions evenly, success measured as conversions count.
contingency.thenB: Design prioritises larger transactions first, success measured as value or revenue converted.
contingency.ifUnknown: Assume count of conversions is the working measure, since that is the simpler default, and flag that this should be revisited once they can state a value preference.

questions.text: Have you noticed any pattern in who already converts purchases to EMI today, or is that something you don't track yet?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: If they've seen a pattern, I use it to decide who to prioritise and what message angle fits.
contingency.ifB: If nobody tracks it, I treat it as unknown and design the run itself to surface a split, using at least two different plausible explanations.
contingency.thenA: Build around the stated pattern as a working segment hypothesis.
contingency.thenB: Design a broader first run with built-in tracking to learn the pattern rather than guessing it.
contingency.ifUnknown: Treat as unknown and design to learn it from this run.

questions.text: Why do you think most EMI-eligible purchases are not being converted right now?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: If they name a specific reason (cost perception, unawareness of eligibility, friction in the conversion flow), the messages address that reason directly.
contingency.ifB: If they say they genuinely don't know, I carry it as an open barrier and the first message copy stays broad/awareness-based rather than targeted at one guess.
contingency.thenA: Message content and CTA built around the stated barrier.
contingency.thenB: Message content stays general awareness plus prompt, with the run designed to surface the real barrier.
contingency.ifUnknown: Assume low awareness of eligibility as the working default, lightly stated, not acted on exclusively.

questions.text: Beyond transaction size, have you noticed any difference by purchase category or merchant type — for example electronics, travel, appliances versus everyday spend — in who ends up converting to EMI? Or is that not something you've tracked?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: If a category pattern exists, I'd tailor the message to lead with that category's typical use-case (e.g. 'split your big electronics bill') and prioritise sends around purchases in that category.
contingency.ifB: If no pattern is known or tracked, I'd write the message generically around ticket size and recent purchase, and treat category as something this first run can help surface rather than something we design against now.
contingency.ifUnknown: I'll treat category as unknown and design the messaging around ticket size and recency only, flagging category as something worth watching once this run has data.

limitations: Stated as unavailable by the user: We want more EMI-eligible card purchases to become EMI. We have no campaign history. I need a 7 day plan.

dimensions.name: Transaction ticket size
dimensions.rationale: Manager-observed gap (₹10k+ converts more) is the one concrete pattern available; since this is a belief about cause that the manager cannot independently verify, I am not asking them to pick between explanations. I'm carrying it into the design as a message variant by band, and the first run's band-by-band conversion data will itself test whether the belief holds.
dimensions.note: Used to split messaging (fee/interest framing for ≥₹10,000, ease/simplicity framing for under ₹10,000) rather than to include/exclude anyone — both bands remain in the eligible audience. This is the user's own explanation, carried as a hypothesis: it has not been tested and competing explanations may remain.

dimensions.name: Purchase category or merchant type
dimensions.rationale: Could in principle segment messaging if certain categories (electronics, travel) converted differently.
dimensions.note: Manager has not noticed any pattern here and does not track it ('nothing as of now'). Closing this as a segmentation axis for this run: the audience is cut by eligibility and ticket size only. If category data emerges from this run or elsewhere, it becomes a candidate for a later run.
